item.title: Romania shuts nuclear plant, Hungary dams dry Danube River
item.description: Romania has shut down its only nuclear plant in a rare move prompted by the lack of cooling water from the Danube River. Hungary, meanwhile, is racing to dam the Danube, trying to keep its Paks plant online.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Kennedy Center board approves Trump name on facade, renovation plan
item.description: The move appears designed to circumvent a judge's ruling that the US president's name should be removed, potentially setting the stage for a new legal fight over the Kennedy Center's name and future.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: US disputes reports of trying conditions on carrier in Gulf
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth called reports of poor conditions and mental health strain aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier in the Middle East "completely misrepresented." Senators want an investigation.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: When the earth moves: six major earthquakes of 2026
item.description: Colombia, Venezuela, Mindanao: Thousands have died in powerful earthquakes this year. Six such events show that the magnitude of the quake is not the only factor determining the scale of the disaster.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Israeli military moves as settlers besiege 3 West Bank homes
item.description: Israel's military has moved to try to stop a group of settlers from besieging three homes in the occupied West Bank. One was owned by a Palestinian American, prompting an unusually sharp rebuke from the US ambassador.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Eritrea: a rising power along a global shipping artery
item.description: Amid growing tensions and security risks in the Horn of Africa, Eritrea, with its strategically important coastal points on the Red Sea, is emerging as an important player in the region.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: What would a North Korean troop surge mean for Ukraine war?
item.description: Ukraine is claiming that North Korea is preparing to send tens of thousands more troops to Russia, where they'll gain valuable battlefield experience.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Colombia earthquake: Rescue operation enters 'final phase'
item.description: Rescuers are racing against a critical 72-hour window to find survivors after a magnitude 7.4 earthquake that has killed 265 people, left hundreds missing, and displaced tens of thousands across western Colombia.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: US: Karoline Leavitt to step down as Trump's spokesperson
item.description: White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt is to leave her job at the end of the month, President Donald Trump says. Leavitt, 28, is the youngest-ever person to have held the position.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: How North Korea has profited from its support for Russia
item.description: Exceptionally high revenues, particularly from war aid for Russia, are consolidating the power of North Korea's autocratic leader. A small number of people in the country are benefiting from an economic boom.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Why is Russia's Yabloko party barred from upcoming election?
item.description: Russia's highest court has banned anti-war opposition party Yabloko from September's parliamentary election. What does this mean for the election campaign, opponents of the war and for the political mood in the country?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: 25 years Ohrid Agreement: Is N. Macedonia's peace holding?
item.description: A quarter of a century after the Ohrid Framework Agreement ended North Macedonia's 2001 conflict, analysts warn that peace between ethnic communities remains fragile.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Iran war leaves Iraq running out of money
item.description: Because of the blockage of the Strait of Hormuz, Iraq cannot export enough oil to fund the country's huge public sector. Protests have already started. Will the Iran war destabilize Iraq again?
item.dc:subject: World
